Pool and refresh sensitivity

Source: vignettes/pool-sensitivity.Rmd
pool-sensitivity.Rmd

Were the pool hyperparameters ever varied?

The default configuration fixes m=20m = 20, y=3m=60y = 3m = 60, B=150B = 150, with an ≈8×\approx 8\times calibration saving over a full grid search. The von Neumann lens demands scenarios: we sweep m∈{5,10,20,40,80}m \in \{5,10,20,40,80\}, y/m∈{1,2,3,5,10}y/m \in \{1,2,3,5,10\}, B∈{60,120,240}B \in \{60,120,240\} and measure best QQ — and, crucially, the lex-decisive fraction: how often the HH tie-break actually changed the incumbent.

Generated. 2026-05-30, lcdaGRASP 0.3.0, 5 reps on SBM(300, 5 blocks, p_in=0.12, p_out=0.02).

library(ggplot2); library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
sm <- d$results |>
  group_by(m, y_ratio, B) |>
  summarise(Q = mean(best_Q), H_pct = mean(H_decisive_pct), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(sm, aes(factor(m), factor(y_ratio), fill = Q)) +
  geom_tile() + geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", Q)), size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ B, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(title = "Best Q vs pool size m and refresh ratio y/m",
       x = "pool size m", y = "refresh ratio y/m (3 = paper default)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

ggplot(sm, aes(factor(m), factor(y_ratio), fill = H_pct)) +
  geom_tile() + geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", H_pct)), size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ B, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma") +
  labs(title = "Lex-decisive fraction (%): how often H broke a Q-tie",
       subtitle = "Near 0 => the lexicographic objective is mostly ornamental",
       x = "pool size m", y = "y/m") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

d$results |>
  dplyr::group_by(m, y_ratio, B) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Q = mean(best_Q), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::slice_max(Q, n = 6) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "Top configurations by mean best Q.")

Reading. Best QQ is remarkably flat across mm and y/my/m once BB is moderate — the default (m=20,y/m=3)(m=20, y/m=3) is reasonable but not uniquely best, and small pools are competitive at lower cost. The lex-decisive fraction is typically near zero, empirically showing that the lexicographic HH tie-break rarely binds in continuous QQ space.

References

  • Prais, M., & Ribeiro, C. C. (2000). Reactive GRASP. INFORMS J. Comput., 12(3), 164–176. doi:10.1287/ijoc.12.3.164.12639
